summary: Feed s148_double to IDS is degraded: 24.5% duplicate packets (617/2516) and 100% missing VLAN tags for required VLANs 10,20. Duplicates waste IDS capacity and distort detection; stripped VLANs blind IDS to segment context.

findings.root_cause: Systematic duplication in visibility layer - packet broker aggregating overlapping SPAN/mirror sessions or TAP+SPAN feeds covering same traffic without deduplication, or a looped aggregation. 24.5% duplicates is far above 5% threshold and indicates broker-level duplication, not normal TCP retransmits.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS reprocesses same packets, wasting CPU and 1G port capacity, inflating flow/alert counts, risking state-table exhaustion and false positives, and can cause the IDS to miss real attacks while busy with duplicates.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (packet hash window ~5ms) on the aggregation to drop identical packets before delivery to IDS, restoring 1:1 traffic view and freeing IDS capacity for real detection.

findings.root_cause: 802.1Q tags stripped before IDS - broker is popping VLAN tags on ingress/egress or SPAN source is configured as access port instead of trunk. 100% untagged while VLANs 10 and 20 are required proves systematic tag removal.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses segmentation context for VLANs 10 and 20, cannot apply VLAN-aware detection policies, misses VLAN-hopping and inter-VLAN lateral movement, and has zero visibility into those required segments.

recommended_fix.why: Configure broker and SPAN/trunk to retain and forward 802.1Q tags for VLANs 10,20 end-to-end to the IDS so it receives correctly tagged traffic for accurate segmentation and coverage.
